executiveSummary: Maashorst's official/generated 2025 identity, 59,671 residents, 39 neighbourhoods, six districts, six BAG woonplaatsen, 44 BRT settlement labels, ten logical road-border routes, 76 scheduled-transit stop areas and Bernhoven's public acute-care record are substantially coherent. Neighbourhood rows total 59,690 residents, nineteen above the municipal control (+0.032%), which the allocator reconciles without rewriting the published observations. All ten canonical presets execute deterministically at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across eight services with finite bounds, exact no-event behavior, causal-ledger closure, service-layer invariance and monotone event-attributable burden. Release is nevertheless correction-required. The generic river scenario asserts an exact 1.566633 m municipal flood depth from T+12 through T+72, 29,655 affected people-equivalent and 1,967,962.626 deprived person-hours at T+72, although the municipality's official environmental assessment treats flooding from large waters as a comparatively limited local mechanism and highlights intense-rain drainage, heat and drought instead. The canonical wildfire is a remote Veluwe smoke exercise with no local flame, while De Maashorst is a large contiguous forest/heath area for which six authorities signed a specific wildfire-control plan after the 700-hectare 2020 Peel fire. Moving the synthetic ignition to the official Buitengebied Maashorst neighbourhood produces flame but still ranks that source neighbourhood only sixth, behind urban neighbourhoods. Eight materially different nonzero single-hazard runs reuse the exact same complete neighbourhood order. The named Groningen earthquake almost disappears locally even though KNMI documents the Peelrand fault and the damaging 1932 Uden earthquake; a selectable local diagnostic produces large but entirely uncalibrated motion, proving only that source choice matters. Public registers provide one Volkel weather station, 204 partial water assets, one electricity-planning sample, 94 antenna records, 37 education locations and Bernhoven context, but not live topology, state, backup, capacity or restoration. The A50/N264/N324 and dispersed villages, no in-boundary rail station, Volkel Air Base and public aviation/hazardous-material risk categories, high groundwater along faults, Haps wastewater dependence for Zeeland/Odiliapeel, care access and first-72-hour resources require explicit event and action evidence. Unknown incident, utility, road, airfield, care, support-point and household-preparedness states remain Unknown or NoData, never safe or zero.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM1991 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, woonplaats and settlement inputs
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated CBS/BAG/BRT snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; audited 3 September 2026
supports: The annual official/generated row identifies GM1991 as Maashorst and reports 59,671 residents, density 435/km², 23.2% aged 65-plus and 9,126 one-person households. CBS/PDOK context is CC BY 4.0 and demographic context, not incident-time occupancy or individual vulnerability.

The municipality reference point [5.655765894781626,51.68784692099713] lies inside the generalized 2025 boundary. The administrative outline is suitable for selection and aggregation, not terrain, groundwater, sewer, forest, plume, route or asset connectivity.

Thirty-nine neighbourhood rows across six districts sum to 59,690 residents (+19, +0.032%), 26,395 households and 13,855 independently rounded residents aged 65-plus. The simulator reconciles population to the municipal control without silently treating the publication difference as zero people.

BAG supplies Odiliapeel, Reek, Schaijk, Uden, Volkel and Zeeland; BRT supplies 44 locality labels including 20 buurtschappen, eight deelkernen, nine gehuchten and seven woonkernen. BAG/PDOK is Public Domain Mark 1.0 and BRT is CC BY 4.0; polygons, labels and CBS rows retain separate provenance and meaning.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Official environmental assessment, climate mechanisms and preparedness context
evidenceSources.edition: Omgevingseffectrapport Omgevingsvisie Maashorst, adopted-plan attachment dated 21 November 2023; current municipal crisis pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The official assessment treats flooding from large waters as a comparatively limited municipal risk because Maashorst is distant from large water bodies; it instead identifies intense-rain drainage, heat and drought as material local mechanisms and describes heavily paved urban Uden as vulnerable to heat and drainage pressure. Its 140 mm rain map is a static stress scenario, not a live forecast or observed footprint.

The assessment and municipal context distinguish elevated sandy terrain, urban paving, water nuisance, groundwater, drought, heat and nature. They do not publish a municipality-wide major-river depth, selected breach, probability or T+12–T+72 recession curve.

The municipal crisis page and meterkast card direct residents to official alerts and named electricity, drinking-water and telecom channels and ask for emergency-kit/business-continuity preparation. Guidance is not measurement of household stock, support-point readiness, utility state or guaranteed assistance within 72 hours.

The PDF is official static planning evidence with a stated document date; the municipal web pages are retrieval-time guidance. No standard machine update cadence or reuse licence is stated, so neither can be silently promoted to current incident state.

evidenceSources.publisher: Waterschap Aa en Maas / Het Waterschapshuis
evidenceSources.title: E03 — Maashorst groundwater, wijst, urban drainage, wastewater and partial water-asset evidence
evidenceSources.edition: Current water-board pages and 29 January 2025 groundwater report inspected 3 September 2026; HWH asset snapshot retrieved 3 September 2026
supports: Aa en Maas describes Maashorst as high sandy terrain where exceptionally wet 2023–2024 conditions filled subsurface storage, natural drainage is limited and impermeable faults create wijst: groundwater can emerge on the high side and affect fields, gardens and cellars. High terrain is therefore not equivalent to no groundwater nuisance.

The water board's Sint Annabos project says the Bitswijkseloop drains a large part of urban Uden and combines measures for drought and water nuisance. The 29 January 2025 report says the board has limited control over groundwater and that precise fault behavior remains under investigation; both are dated context, not current municipality-wide status.

The partial HWH assignment contains 204 points in GM1991: 196 weirs, two surface-water pumps and six wastewater pumps. Named registrations include Reek, Schaijk, Zeeland, Odiliapeel and De Peel, but many function/capacity fields are null; contributor-dependent CC BY-SA 4.0 points do not establish completeness, connectivity, units, telemetry, power, backup or live operation.

A November 2025 power failure at the Haps wastewater plant prompted Aa en Maas to ask residents and businesses to reduce wastewater and reported overflows; the plant serves Zeeland and Odiliapeel in Maashorst. This is an authoritative historical cross-boundary dependency example, not evidence of a current outage or of every Maashorst catchment.

evidenceSources.publisher: Waterschap Aa en Maas / Gemeenten Maashorst, Bernheze en Oss / Veiligheidsregio Brabant-Noord / Staatsbosbeheer
evidenceSources.title: E04 — Official De Maashorst wildfire-control plan and landscape mechanism
evidenceSources.edition: Plan signed 25 February and public notice published 5 March 2026; current De Maashorst area page inspected 3 September 2026
supports: Six public partners signed a specific dynamic plan to prevent a fire in De Maashorst from becoming uncontrollable. The notice cites the 2020 Peel fire of about 700 hectares—roughly one fifth of De Maashorst—and treats water retention and drought reduction as structural fire prevention.

Aa en Maas describes De Maashorst as Noord-Brabant's largest contiguous nature area, with forest, heath and drift-sand landscapes and the Peelrand fault/wijst transition. This is direct local wildfire/fuel/access/water context, not a statement that a fire is currently burning.

The plan establishes owners and a locally material mechanism but does not expose a machine-readable ignition likelihood, live perimeter, fuel moisture, visitor count, suppression-water availability, road closure, crew position or recovery status.

The public notice and area page state publication/retrieval time but no standard reuse licence or operational update cadence. A simulation must separately label static landscape, official planning, observation, forecast and selected exercise event.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Peelrand fault and historical Uden earthquake evidence
evidenceSources.edition: KNMI historical explanation and natural-earthquake knowledge page inspected 3 September 2026; KNMI observation snapshot 2 September 2026
supports: KNMI says southern Netherlands natural seismicity is associated with faults around the Roerdalslenk, including the Peelrand fault. It documents a magnitude 5 earthquake near Uden in 1932 that caused damage around Uden and Veghel, and a magnitude 3.4 Mariahout event in 1999 on the same fault.

This is authoritative historical and geological evidence, not a forecast, recurrence probability, current warning, expected magnitude or local ground-motion/fragility surface. A named Groningen-source exercise and a selected local tectonic event are different scenarios.

Volkel Airport is the only KNMI weather station inside GM1991 in the deployed snapshot. At 2026-09-02T23:30Z it reported temperature 17.2°C, relative humidity 80%, gust 8.14 m/s, no ten-minute rain and visibility 31.1 km; the 10-minute CC BY 4.0 observation is a point/time observation, not a 72-hour forecast or fire-weather field.

No KNMI seismic origin in the deployed 365-day bounding-box snapshot lies inside GM1991. No recent match is NoData/no event in that bounded feed, not proof of zero local seismic hazard or future safety.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — Municipal risk profile, response-coverage planning and Volkel Air Base context
evidenceSources.edition: Municipal page accompanying Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2024–2027; coverage-plan appendices 2024–2027; current Defensie Volkel page inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The public municipal risk page identifies nature fire in Herperduin/De Maashorst, fire in buildings with vulnerable residents, hazardous-material businesses and road transport, an aviation incident at Volkel Air Base, livestock disease and large events as locally relevant categories. Category inclusion is not an event probability or current incident.

The regional plan treats electricity/gas, telecom/ICT and cyber disruption as cross-cutting priorities. The public response-coverage appendices contain planning arrival estimates above ten minutes for several named education, care, hospital and Volkel/Odiliapeel objects; estimates are not live dispatch, staffing, access or outcome guarantees.

Defensie's public page states that Volkel hosts F-35 aircraft and national air tasks; VRBN says a specific airfield incident response plan exists. Public identity supports an aviation/continuity dependency, not disclosure or inference of sensitive operational posture, fuel, munition, security, runway, backup or current readiness.

The risk and coverage documents are official multi-year planning/scenario evidence. No standard redistribution licence or incident update cadence is stated; live alerts, authority decisions and operational resources must be separately sourced and time-bound.

evidenceSources.title: E07 — Road, scheduled-transit and Bernhoven acute-care context
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 1 August 2026; OVapi snapshot retrieved 3 September 2026; RIVM acute-care v1.1 published 3 July 2026; provincial N264 page inspected 3 September 2026
supports: Ten monthly CC0 NWB border-route records connect GM1991 with Oss, Bernheze, Meierijstad, Boekel and Land van Cuijk. A50 sides to Oss/Bernheze/Meierijstad and N324/N277 sides to multiple neighbours are series/shared physical corridors, not independent additive capacity; every 260/150 scenario-unit ceiling is a logical mobility/supply proxy.

N264, N324, N277, N605 and A50 connect dispersed villages and external destinations. The provincial N264 Odiliapeel–Haps page describes substantial agricultural traffic and staged works, demonstrating corridor context without establishing incident-time passability, throughput or detour capacity.

No ProRail station lies in GM1991; 76 in-boundary GTFS stop areas include Uden Busstation and Uden Ziekenhuis. Schedule/reference locations are not live buses, accessible capacity, evacuation transport, responder reachability or continuity.

RIVM acute-care v1.1 CC0 assigns Bernhoven Ziekenhuis in Uden, reporting 24/7 emergency care, acute obstetrics, 21 treatment rooms and 23,225 emergency visits in 2025. A questionnaire and historical annual count do not establish current acceptance, occupancy, staffing, ambulance access, generator/fuel endurance, medicines, water or recovery.

evidenceSources.publisher: Gemeente Maashorst / Enexis / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO / RIVM
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Partial electricity, communication, education, air-quality and preparedness evidence
evidenceSources.edition: Municipal page current 1 July 2026 and inspected 3 September 2026; public-context snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026
supports: The municipality reports an Enexis connection pause in affected northeast-Brabant areas and maximum capacity at the Uden substation. One NBNL postcode sample maps to Enexis area UD Uden and reports planning queues and 19 projects, earliest 2026. Congestion/planning evidence is not a current outage, live load, switching reserve, priority-customer map or restoration trajectory.

RDI assigns 94 installations—four broadcast, seventeen fixed-link, 52 mobile, one other-mobile and twenty amateur—and DUO assigns 37 education records—twenty primary, two secondary, two special and thirteen other registered uses. RDI has no stated standard reuse licence/fixed cadence; DUO is attribution-licensed and daily. Neither proves coverage, backhaul, backup, occupancy, shelter/support role, accessibility, stock or staffing.

No RIVM PM2.5 observation point lies inside GM1991 and no Waterinfo observation/forecast point is municipally assigned in the deployed snapshot. Missing local matches do not mean clean air, zero water stress or forecast safety; regional interpolation requires a governed method, time and uncertainty.

Municipal 72-hour preparedness communication and regional work on emergency support points are programme/guidance evidence. No public source reviewed confirms incident-active support-point locations, capacity, staffing, water, power, communication or accessibility in Maashorst; absence of confirmation remains Unknown, not proof that no arrangement exists.

identity.summary: GM1991, Maashorst, Noord-Brabant and safety region Brabant-Noord agree across official and generated inputs.
notes: Municipality code/name, province, safety-region membership and 2025 demographic edition agree.
The generated municipal reference point lies inside the generalized geometry.
No identity, municipal-control or safety-region contradiction was found.

geography.summary: The administrative geography is coherent, but high sand, faults/wijst, urban drainage and a large nature area require different physical surfaces.
notes: A generalized boundary and municipality centre cannot resolve the Peelrand fault, high/low wijst sides, groundwater storage, Bitswijkseloop catchment, paving, forest fuels or smoke paths.
Official evidence distinguishes urban Uden, De Maashorst/Herperduin, agricultural and dispersed village settings; a shared administrative seed does not.

Relative distance from major waters does not mean zero flood consequence: direct large-river inundation, indirect transport/supply effects, rain, groundwater and wastewater must stay separately typed.

demography.summary: The 2025 municipal control and neighbourhood rows reconcile within independent CBS rounding.
notes: Official/generated population is 59,671, density 435/km², age65-plus share 23.2% and one-person households 9,126.
Neighbourhood population is 59,690 (+19, +0.032%), households 26,395 and independently rounded age65-plus rows 13,855; source observations remain unchanged.
Registered residents exclude incident-time Bernhoven patients/staff, Air Base personnel, pupils, visitors, road users, seasonal workers, responders and evacuees.

regionalDetail.summary: Core neighbourhood statistics are nearly complete, while sparse fields and public infrastructure inventories retain source coverage and NoData.
notes: Core fields cover 39/39 neighbourhoods; average home value covers 37/39, household size and population density 38/39, cars per household 35/39, district heating and public charging 0/39. Null/suppressed fields are not zero.
The 204 water objects, one KNMI station, one NBNL sample, 94 antennas, 37 schools and one acute-care record have different publishers, dates, licences, coverage and evidence classes.
Static point assignment does not prove network service, operational state, incident occupancy, accessibility, backup or restoration.

settlements.summary: Six BAG woonplaatsen and 44 BRT locality labels coherently retain Maashorst's village and dispersed-rural structure.
notes: No BAG woonplaats representative centre lies outside the generalized municipal geometry.
Odiliapeel, Reek, Schaijk, Uden, Volkel and Zeeland remain explicit rather than being reduced to the Uden centre.
Place membership and labels do not establish live population, care dependency, route access or utility continuity.

transport.summary: Logical border routes and scheduled stops cannot establish village, hospital, aviation, evacuation or supply continuity.
notes: Ten road records include repeated series/shared identities on A50, N324 and N277; ceilings are non-additive scenario units affecting mobility and road logistics only.
The graph lacks internal link/junction/bridge state, local forest and Air Base access, closures, agricultural traffic, detours, live buses, vehicles, responders and destinations.
No rail station lies inside GM1991, and Bernhoven's in-boundary location does not prove that ambulances, staff, supplies and referrals can reach it throughout an event.

emergencyContext.summary: Strong local fire, water, aviation, seismic, care and preparedness context exists, but incident selection and first-72-hour readiness remain unconfirmed.
notes: Evidence supports distinct local clocks for rain/sewer/groundwater, drought/fire/smoke, severe weather, a selected tectonic event, aviation/hazardous-material incidents, prolonged utilities/cyber and care disruption.
The 23.2% age65-plus share and 9,126 one-person households support aggregate planning and outreach, not individual targeting or assumptions about self-reliance.
No reviewed public source confirms incident-active Maashorst emergency support points, resource levels, household stock, hospital acceptance, utility restoration or Air Base continuity.
Timestamped KNMI, warning, air, water, road and operator messages remain observation/forecast/replay evidence until explicitly selected with issue, valid and expiry time.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical presets execute at all six mandatory checkpoints for all eight services.
notes: Initial MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM1991 pnpm audit:model passed two tests across severe-storm, pluvial-flood, river-flood, coastal-flood, heatwave, winter-storm, cyberattack, earthquake, wildfire and compound at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 for power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply.
Focused inline Vite runs captured complete checkpoint trajectories, service outputs and neighbourhood ranks without leaving a scratch test file.

These are deterministic exercise indices, modeled people-equivalent and matched-no-event deprived service person-hours—not observations, probabilities, casualties, customers without service, economic loss or operator commitments.

numericalInvariants.summary: Determinism, finite bounds, exact no-event behavior, allocation, reconciliation, causal closure and cumulative-burden contracts pass.
notes: All eight service availability values remain in [0,1], while hazards, demand, delivery, affected people-equivalent and person-hours remain finite and non-negative.
Zero-intensity scenarios return exact zero event hazard, affected population and event-attributable burden; repeats are deterministic and cumulative burden is monotone.
Every service allocates all 39 neighbourhoods and exactly 59,671 residents; demand/delivery reconcile and changing the selected service leaves hazard unchanged.
Arithmetic validity does not validate local hazard physics, route, utility, hospital, aviation, occupancy, intervention or recovery meaning.

spatialPlausibility.summary: Common source-insensitive ranks contradict Maashorst's nature, fault, groundwater, urban-rain, heat and major-river geography.
notes: At T+24 storm, pluvial, river, coastal/wind, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire all reuse the exact complete 39-neighbourhood order, led by Centrum Uden, Verspreide huizen Mun and Zoggel and ending with Schaijk, Eikenheuvel, Buurtschap Hoeven and Verspreide huizen Peel.

A controlled synthetic wildfire moved to the official Buitengebied Maashorst neighbourhood centre [5.6164988021632904,51.68599634220825] produces T+24 fire 0.593566, smoke 0.557871 and 15,406 affected, yet ranks the source neighbourhood sixth behind five other areas. It is a diagnostic, not a real incident or calibrated forecast.

The canonical Groningen earthquake at T+6 yields only 0.002484 g and severity 0.007762; a controlled Uden-centre source yields 0.250771 g and severity 0.783659 at T+3. The latter numbers are unsupported synthetic diagnostics, but the contrast proves that named source choice materially changes output.

packages/sim-core/src/model.ts derives a regional hazard seed from city/scenario/region identifiers without physical disaster family, source containment or evidence surface. Administrative hashes cannot substitute for full-geometry mechanisms.

serviceDependencies.summary: Road-only transfer is correctly scoped, but exact water, wastewater, utility, telecom, hospital, facility and supply states lack causal topology and live evidence.
notes: NWB flows affect mobility and road supply only, avoiding false equivalence with physical utility networks; shared/series road identities and 260/150 capacities remain logical scenario proxies.

HWH points do not connect groundwater, Bitswijkseloop, surface water, sewer, Haps wastewater treatment or potable-water pressure/quality; the historical Haps outage illustrates a real coupled pathway absent from the service graph.
NBNL, RDI, DUO, GTFS, RIVM and Volkel public records do not expose feeders, pipes, backhaul, switching, loads, priority, staff, stock, vehicles, generator endurance, acceptance or restoration.

At river T+72 availability is drainage 0.186827, water 0.396378, facilities 0.403066, telecom 0.452119, power 0.495493, gas 0.682502, mobility 0.707187 and supply 0.722423. No operator or authority validates these exact values.

causalTrace.summary: The arithmetic ledger closes, but event identity, evidence time and accountable 0–72-hour decisions are absent from the causal graph.
notes: Hazard contributions sum to severity, service-stage contributions reconstruct availability and municipality pressure closes numerically.

River selects no source river/gauge, defence/breach, official scenario, terrain footprint, depth/velocity/arrival/recession or uncertainty; wildfire selects remote Veluwe smoke rather than a De Maashorst event; earthquake is named for Groningen rather than a local tectonic source.
Trace does not select rain duration/catchment/sewer/groundwater state, Haps treatment status, fire perimeter/fuels/plume, road/hospital/airfield state, utility target, warning or incident authority.

T+0–6 needs detection, evidence selection, warnings and coordination; T+6–24 fire/evacuation/closure/care/utility decisions; T+24–48 verified access, water, hospital, welfare and restoration state; T+48–72 hotspot/re-ignition, repair, resupply, re-entry and unresolved-needs review.

recovery72h.summary: Persistent consequences are useful conservatism, but exact plateaus and recoveries are not tied to Maashorst events, owners, resources or verified actions.
notes: River floodDepthM/severity remains exactly 1.566633/0.486771 from T+12 through T+72, affected remains 29,655 from T+24 through T+72 and burden reaches 1,967,962.626 person-hours without selected hydraulics or an official local footprint.

Compound floodDepthM remains 0.525716 T+12–T+72; severity declines 0.949875 to 0.502726, affected rises 31,703 to 31,840 and burden reaches 2,106,949.189, while T+72 telecom is 0.283711 and water 0.357149 without operator calibration.

Storm/pluvial/winter forcing can disappear while modeled service burden continues. That is conceptually valid, but groundwater, sewer overflow, fallen trees, access, fire hotspots, wastewater, care backlog and repairs require distinct evidence-backed clocks.

Preparedness guidance, a signed wildfire plan and multi-year risk/coverage documents do not themselves confirm that alerts, support points, crews, water, beds, fuel, stock or repairs were available and completed in the selected 72-hour run.

findings.summary: Eight materially different nonzero single-hazard scenarios reuse one complete neighbourhood ranking.
findings.evidence: At T+24 storm, pluvial, river, coastal/wind, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire all rank all 39 neighbourhoods identically, led by Centrum Uden, Verspreide huizen Mun and Zoggel. The common seed omits physical hazard family and evidence surface, contradicting E02–E05's urban rain/heat, fault/groundwater, local nature-fire and earthquake mechanisms.
findings.action: V3 release gate: replace the common rank with hazard-specific full-geometry surfaces and explicit coverage/NoData. Add regressions that different mechanisms need not share an order and source-containing/covered cells govern direct impact; retain service-layer invariance.

findings.summary: The major-river preset asserts an unsupported deep municipal flood contrary to local official mechanism prioritisation.
findings.evidence: E02 describes major-water flooding as comparatively limited locally and highlights rain, drainage, heat and drought. The model selects no river, gauge, defence failure or official footprint but holds floodDepthM 1.566633 T+12–T+72, reports 29,655 affected and 1,967,962.626 person-hours at T+72, and applies a hash-derived footprint.
findings.action: Suppress GM1991's local metre, affected, service and map claims in the canonical river preset. Re-enable only for an expert-selected versioned LIWO/RWS/water-board scenario with source, defence/breach, probability, footprint, depth/arrival/recession, uncertainty and NoData; retain separately labeled indirect regional transport/supply effects.

findings.summary: The remote wildfire preset misses Maashorst's primary direct fire mechanism and fails a local source-containment diagnostic.
findings.evidence: E04 documents the official De Maashorst wildfire-control plan and 2020 Peel-fire scale. Canonical T+24 has zero local flame, smoke 0.366870 and 1,475 affected from a Veluwe source. A synthetic source placed in Buitengebied Maashorst generates fire 0.593566 yet ranks its source neighbourhood only sixth; those values diagnose model behavior and are not incident claims.
findings.action: Add selectable local ignition/perimeter scenarios driven by authoritative land cover/fuel, drought/moisture, wind/plume, visitors, access, suppression-water and action state. Enforce containment/distance behavior before operational use; retain the Veluwe preset only as a clearly remote-smoke exercise.

findings.summary: A Groningen-named remote exercise cannot stand in for Maashorst's natural Peelrand-fault scenario.
findings.evidence: E05 documents the Peelrand fault and damaging 1932 Uden event. Canonical T+6 motion is 0.002484 g; a controlled Uden-centre diagnostic reaches 0.250771 g at T+3. The diagnostic is not a plausible forecast or calibration, but proves source selection matters and that either number is unsafe to present without official event/ground-motion/site/fragility evidence.
findings.action: Retain the Groningen preset as remote exercise only. Add a separately named natural-tectonic scenario with KNMI event/source, versioned ground-motion and site-response surface, building/infrastructure fragility, uncertainty and valid time; suppress local damage/service precision until calibrated.

findings.summary: Generic water/drainage scores collapse rain, groundwater/wijst, surface water, sewer, wastewater and potable-water states.
findings.evidence: E02/E03 distinguish paved Uden rain pressure, high sandy storage, impermeable faults/wijst, Bitswijkseloop, partial water assets and the Haps wastewater dependency. Pluvial T+24 still reports exact drainage 0.498368 and water 0.712345, while 204 HWH points have no complete topology or live state.
findings.action: Split rain/surface-water drainage, groundwater, sewer conveyance/overflow, wastewater treatment and potable pressure/quantity/quality/advisory. Keep HWH and historical Haps evidence typed and partial; ingest catchments, topology and live state only with operator authority. Null, uncovered and unavailable state stays Unknown.

findings.summary: Border-road proxies and scheduled stops cannot establish dispersed-village, Bernhoven, forest or airfield access.
findings.evidence: E07 shows A50/N264/N324/N277/N605 dependencies, no local rail station, 76 static transit stops and Bernhoven in Uden. Repeated/shared corridors are non-additive; the model lacks internal junction, closure, detour, bus/vehicle, agricultural traffic, ambulance, referral, destination and incident-access state.
findings.action: Build internal multimodal reachability from NWB/BGT and authoritative closure/NDW/operator inputs with issue/valid/expiry time. Route residents, assisted evacuation, responders, hospital staff/supplies, fire suppression, Air Base response and logistics separately; capacity and accessibility remain Unknown until confirmed.

findings.summary: Exact utility, telecom, hospital, facility and supply trajectories lack operational topology, backup and restoration evidence.
findings.evidence: One electricity-planning sample, 94 antennas, 37 education records, one hospital questionnaire and public Air Base identity are context only. They do not expose complete causal topology, live state, backhaul, priority, staff, stock, fuel, switching, acceptance or restoration. Exact T+72 river/compound availability has no operator validation.
findings.action: Keep service values visibly synthetic with uncertainty. Ingest only operator-authorized zones, dependencies and restoration ranges with publisher/version/time/coverage/licence and affectsSimulation. Never infer sensitive Volkel topology or promote planning territories/public points to operational flow.

findings.summary: The first-72-hour view lacks an accountable action/resource ledger for wildfire, water, care, access and utilities.
findings.evidence: E02/E04/E06/E08 provide preparedness and planning context but not incident-active support points, warnings, crews, suppression water, hospital acceptance, household stock, emergency water, utility repair or re-entry. Exact affected/recovery trajectories therefore cannot be attributed to confirmed decisions or resources.
findings.action: At each checkpoint expose proposed/requested/confirmed/completed/cancelled actions with owner, authority, trigger, source, issue/valid/expiry, geography, dependency, capacity/resource, confidence, verification and rollback. Do not display a school, hospital, municipal building or support point role unless incident-confirmed.

findings.summary: Publicly identified aviation, hazardous-material, livestock-disease and event pathways are outside the canonical ten scenarios.
findings.evidence: E06 explicitly identifies Volkel aviation, hazardous-material establishments/road transport, animal disease and large events. None should be hidden inside generic compound, wildfire, cyber or facilities scores; public risk eligibility is not current incident probability, and sensitive operational detail is neither needed nor inferred.
findings.action: For later scope, add separately governed aviation/hazardous-material plume/exclusion, livestock/agricultural and crowd scenarios using authorized incident, wind, access and response evidence. Until then render Not modeled/Unknown, not safe or normal.

findings.summary: Storm, coastal/wind, heat/drought, winter, cyber and compound remain uncalibrated planning screens.
findings.evidence: Official evidence supports severe weather, heat/drought and utility/cyber planning, while direct North Sea inundation is not a local Maashorst mechanism. Coastal T+24 has zero water but 21.648 m/s wind; cyber has no named target; compound mixes unrelated assumptions. Volkel's single observation cannot calibrate a 72-hour municipality field.
findings.action: Retain as visibly synthetic exercises, separate direct local from remote/upstream impact, and require valid-time KNMI/replay, selected cyber target and hazard-specific surfaces/actions before operational claims. Zero, Unknown, stale and not-applicable remain distinct.

findings.summary: Sparse publication fields and absent monitoring/operational registers require explicit multi-state semantics.
findings.evidence: District heating and charging cover 0/39 neighbourhoods; several CBS fields are incomplete; no local RIVM PM2.5, Waterinfo or recent seismic point is assigned; HWH is partial; NBNL/RDI/DUO/RIVM do not prove operation. These differ from modeled zero coastal water or zero T+24 ground motion.
findings.action: Use one map/API/export contract for observed/modeled value including zero, Unknown/not covered, stale/expired and not applicable. Show publisher, edition, issue/valid/retrieval, units, coverage, completeness, licence, confidence and affectsSimulation; test empty intersections/nulls never render safe/normal/zero.

findings.summary: The deterministic numerical and semantic contract passes for GM1991 on the audited build.
findings.evidence: The focused harness passes ten presets, six checkpoints and eight services. Values are finite/bounded, zero-event behavior exact, all 39 neighbourhoods and 59,671 residents reconcile, demand/delivery and causal ledgers close, service selection leaves hazard unchanged, road flows stay within logical capacity and cumulative burden is monotone.

residualLimitations: This is a deterministic first-72-hour planning stress test, not a KNMI, Aa en Maas, Veiligheidsregio Brabant-Noord, Defensie, municipality, hospital or operator forecast, warning, probability, incident declaration, casualty estimate or restoration promise.

The municipality boundary and centre do not resolve Peelrand-fault geometry, wijst sides, groundwater, catchments, sewer pipes, buildings, paving, forest fuels, plumes, roads, assets, households or individuals.
No expert-selected major-river source, gauge/hydrograph, defence state, breach/overtopping, versioned footprint, probability, depth/velocity/arrival/recession or NoData mask is ingested for GM1991.
The 1.566633 floodDepthM and normalized stress are synthetic screening values contrary to local mechanism prioritisation and must not drive evacuation, route, care or service thresholds.
CBS neighbourhood values are rounded/suppressed; the +19 population difference and absent district-heat/charging values are publication semantics, not extra/zero people or assets.
HWH is partial and its 204 points do not establish complete topology, compatible capacity units, connectivity, control, live operation, power dependence, backup or restoration; null remains Unknown.

The Haps outage is a historical example and does not establish current wastewater state or every municipal catchment; groundwater reports likewise describe dated conditions and uncertainty, not T+0 status.
Canonical wildfire lacks local ignition/perimeter, authoritative fuel/moisture, visitor/access, wind/plume and suppression state; the local-source run is an uncalibrated model diagnostic.

Canonical earthquake is a remote Groningen exercise; KNMI historical geology does not provide a current probability, and the controlled Uden-source g values are not official ground motion or damage estimates.
One Volkel weather observation is not a municipal field or 72-hour forecast; no local PM2.5, Waterinfo or recent seismic match is not zero exposure, water stress, event probability or safety.
No complete public causal Enexis feeder/switching, Brabant Water pipe/pressure/quality, gas district, municipal sewer, telecom backhaul or operator restoration topology is authorized in the model.
One NBNL postcode sample is planning/queue context rather than municipal coverage, current load, customer outage, reserve, switching or restoration.
RDI installations do not establish radio/mobile coverage, traffic, backhaul, power/backup, damage, availability or restoration; standard licence and cadence are unstated.

NWB and GTFS are static context and do not establish incident-time roads, buses, throughput, evacuation, responder, hospital, fire-suppression or logistics continuity; shared corridor records are not additive capacity.
RIVM Bernhoven questionnaire data and annual visits do not establish present occupancy, acceptance, staffing, ambulance access, diversion, medicines, water, generator fuel or recovery.
DUO locations do not establish command, reception, shelter, care or distribution roles; no incident-active support-point network/capacity was confirmed in the reviewed public evidence.
Public Volkel identity and risk-plan categories do not authorize inference of sensitive operational topology, fuel, munitions, security, readiness, backup or continuity.
Cyber lacks a named target, architecture, attack path and detection/containment state; coastal is a wind exercise rather than direct North Sea inundation; compound combines unvalidated assumptions.
Aviation, hazardous-material, livestock-disease, agricultural and crowd/event pathways are not represented by current hazard/service vocabulary and must remain Not modeled/Unknown.
Household 72-hour guidance is a preparedness horizon, not measured stock, guaranteed aid arrival, equality of access or a recovery deadline.

Event-attributable essential-service person-hours is a matched-no-event weighted availability proxy, not measured customer outage-hours, simultaneous deprivation, casualties, displacement or welfare loss; six-hour checkpoints can miss rapid change and 72 hours excludes prolonged drought, fire recovery, contamination and reconstruction.
